subject: DPA: model training definition & EU->US transfer path
messages:
From: Asha Menon <asha.menon@mediliumhealth.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement - Medilium <procurement@medilium.com>, Legal - Medilium <legal@medilium.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 09:12:00 +0100
Subject: DPA redlines — carve-out for model training + transfer requirements

Hannah — thanks for taking this on. Attached are our redlines (DPA_redlines_v3.docx) and a short checklist from our security team. High-level asks: 

- We need an explicit carve-out: "Customer Data" (defined below) shall not be used to train, improve, or adapt Redwood's models or model weights. This includes fine-tuning, prompt-tuning, gradient updates, or any other supervised/unsupervised training.
- Minimal telemetry (e.g., API errors, anonymized aggregate metrics) is OK for service health, but only in fully aggregated form and not linkable back to our org.
- EU-origin personal data cannot be transferred to the US unless there is a lawful transfer mechanism (SCCs or adequacy). Please confirm the path you propose.
- Please provide the current subprocessors list and confirm whether any subprocessors process EU data outside the EEA.

We prefer to finalize via DocuSign once redlines are agreed. Procurement is ready to execute but needs a clear SCC/transfer plan and the updated subprocessor appendix.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if helpful.

— Asha Menon
Director, Privacy & Compliance
Medilium Health
attachments: DPA_redlines_v3.docx, Medilium_MAAP_checklist.xlsx

Subject: Re: DPA redlines — carve-out for model training + transfer requirements

Hi Asha — thanks for the clear summary and the checklist. Looping in Neha (legal) and Karthik (sales) to propose language and confirm commercial impact. Quick answers up front: 

- We can propose a strongly-scoped carve-out for Customer Data to prevent direct use for model training. We typically allow aggregated telemetry for service health — we'll propose clear limits on what is considered "aggregated" and retention windows.
- For EU transfers, our standard approach is SCCs (we use the EU SCCs + supplementary measures where needed). I asked Legal to confirm whether any subprocessors currently require transfers outside the EEA.
- We'll prepare an updated subprocessor appendix and a DocuSign envelope once wording is agreed.

Neha / Karthik: can you review Asha's redlines (attached) and return proposed edits by EOD today? Procurement would like a DocuSign-ready DPA for signature next week if possible.

Hannah
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Asha Menon <asha.menon@mediliumhealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 13:21:00 +0100
Subject: Re: DPA redlines — carve-out for model training + transfer requirements

Thanks, Hannah / Asha — I reviewed the redlines. Below is the consolidated proposal from Legal that aims to balance Medilium's privacy needs with our product requirements: 

Proposed clause (high level):
"Customer Content" means all data and content supplied by Customer to the Services. Redwood will not use Customer Content to train, fine-tune, or improve Redwood's model weights or base models. Redwood may process aggregated, de-identified service metrics (e.g., aggregate latency, error rates, token volumes) for the purpose of service monitoring and product analytics provided such metrics are irreversibly aggregated and cannot be re-identified to Customer.

- We will add a definitional appendix that clarifies "de-identified" and provides examples of allowable telemetry.
- For transfers: Redwood will rely on the EU Commission's Standard Contractual Clauses (Module Two) for onward transfers from the EEA to the US and will document supplementary technical and organizational measures (encryption at rest/in transit, KMS controls, access rules). We will provide the SCCs PDF and an updated subprocessor list (see attachments).
- Subprocessors: current list attached; any new subprocessors that would process EU Customer Content will be notified 30 days in advance.
- Execution: we can set up a DocuSign envelope; Legal requests a 10-business-day review window for any late comments.

Open items for commercial:
- Carve-out may impact our ability to run certain quality-improvement programs that rely on customer interactions. Karthik, can you confirm whether this affects the committed SLAs or pricing?
- If Medilium needs narrow exceptions (e.g., a pilot where de-identified samples are used under explicit consent), we can include a Contract Addendum process.

I'll attach a clean DPA prepared with the above language (DPA_redlines_v3 -> DPA_consolidated_v1). If that looks acceptable we can proceed to DocuSign.

— Neha Kapoor
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference
attachments: SCCs_2020.pdf

Appreciate the quick turnaround, Neha. A few commercial notes for Medilium / Hannah: 

- Pricing/credits: because the carve-out restricts certain model improvement programs, we typically offer either (a) a small one-time onboarding credit or (b) a modest discount on committed volume for the first 6 months. For MED-2247 I recommend offering a 10% credit on the first monthly invoice; happy to finalize if Legal confirms the wording.
- SLA impact: none expected for latency or availability. Some advanced feature roadmaps (e.g., custom model tuning) will be unavailable unless Medilium agrees to an opt-in addendum.
- Timeline: if Legal and Medilium sign off on Neha's consolidated DPA today, we can push the DocuSign envelope tomorrow and aim for procurement signature by next Thursday (11/12).

Asha — does that timeline work for you? If procurement wants the credit reflected in the MSA amendment, we should loop in Finance.

Thanks,
Karthik
